name: Talmon
overview: Talmon was a male Levite who served as one of the gatekeepers, a role of responsibility and service in the temple community. His position is noted in several Old Testament books, indicating his involvement in the care and security of the temple. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Talmon likely means 'brightness,' which may reflect a characteristic or hoped-for quality. This proper name is mentioned explicitly in 1 Chronicles 9:17 without indication of divine origin.
familyAndRelationships: Talmon is identified as a descendant of Korah, linking him to a notable Levitical family line. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond this lineage and his role as a gatekeeper.
scriptureSignificance: Talmon's significance lies in his service as a gatekeeper, a critical function in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple worship. His Levitical heritage and connection to Korah situate him within a respected priestly tradition. His mention across multiple Old Testament books underscores the continuity and importance of temple service roles in Israel's religious life.
